content.description: Cloud-based identity and access management service providing SSO, MFA, conditional access, and identity governance for users, groups, and applications.
Service that enforces organizational standards by evaluating resources against rules and policies, denying non-compliant deployments or flagging existing resources for remediation.
Massively scalable object storage for unstructured data such as documents, images, videos, backups, and logs. Supports hot, cool, cold, and archive tiers.
Fully managed file shares in the cloud accessible via SMB and NFS protocols. Used for lift-and-shift workloads, shared application settings, and cross-platform file access.
Service for deploying and managing a group of identical, load-balanced VMs that automatically scale in or out based on demand or schedule.
Run individual containers without managing servers or orchestrators. Per-second billing, fast startup, ideal for short-lived workloads, build agents, and event-driven tasks.
Provides secure RDP and SSH access to virtual machines directly through the Azure portal over TLS, without exposing the VM's public IP address.
Layer-7 (HTTP/HTTPS) regional load balancer with URL-path routing, SSL termination, cookie-based session affinity, and an integrated Web Application Firewall.
Centralized data store and query engine for log and telemetry data from Azure resources and external systems. Queries are written in Kusto Query Language (KQL).
Disaster recovery service that replicates Azure VMs, on-prem VMs, and physical servers to a secondary region for orchestrated failover during region or datacenter outages.

The foundational private network in Azure. Lets resources such as VMs and databases communicate securely with each other, the internet, and on-premises networks. Your own isolated network segment in the cloud.
A subnet- or NIC-level firewall with inbound/outbound rules that allow or deny traffic based on source, destination, port, and protocol.

Layer-4 (TCP/UDP) regional load balancer that distributes inbound traffic across multiple backend VMs. Comes in Public (internet-facing) and Internal (in-VNet) flavors for high availability and scale-out.
Layer-7 (HTTP/HTTPS) load balancer with URL path routing, host-header routing, cookie-based affinity, SSL termination, and an integrated Web Application Firewall.
Hosted DNS service that resolves domain names to IP addresses. Supports public zones (internet-facing) and private zones (resolution within VNets only).
Encrypted IPsec/IKE tunnels between an Azure VNet and on-premises networks (Site-to-Site) or individual devices (Point-to-Site) over the public internet.
Private, dedicated connection from on-premises to Azure — not over the public internet. Higher reliability, lower latency, and consistent bandwidth versus VPN. Enterprise hybrid connectivity.
Secure RDP and SSH access to VMs through the Azure portal, with no public IP exposure on the VM. Sits inside the VNet as a managed jump host.
Fully managed cloud-native firewall at the VNet perimeter. Supports application rules (FQDNs), network rules, NAT rules, and threat intelligence. Cross-VNet scope, more powerful than NSGs.

Networking service that unifies routing, VPN, and ExpressRoute into a single managed hub. Used for large-scale branch-to-branch and branch-to-Azure connectivity. Replaces manually-built hub-spoke topologies.
